title: Capacity drain timetable and safe-evacuation guide for GPU driver rollouts (Q4 2025)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is the canonical operational plan for performing GPU driver upgrades and associated kernel/firmware changes in Q4 2025 with minimal customer impact. It focuses on safe capacity drains, phased rotations across regions and GPU pools, and observable rollback criteria. Use this as the single source for runbook steps, schedule, and comms templates.

Scope and constraints:
- Applies to hosted and dedicated GPU pools in: us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1, asia-southeast-1.
- Affects: inference-worker nodes and node-local drivers (NVIDIA driver 560 -> 570 candidate), host-kernel micro-updates.
- Does NOT include Private (on-prem) customers unless opted into managed driver upgrade.
- Maintenance windows: target low-traffic hours in each region (local early morning).
- SLA: target <0.5% token-drop anomaly and <2% request error delta vs baseline.

High-level approach:
1) Canary phase: pick a small isolated pool (10 GPUs across 2 racks) in us-west-2 to validate node image, driver + runtime kernel combos.
2) Verification: run smoke suites, sample customer workloads, and synthetic load for 2x expected concurrency.
3) Regional ramp: parallel drains limited by regional capacity guardrails (see capacity matrix below).
4) Global completion: when all regions report green and no regressions for 48 hours, finalize.

Capacity guardrails and drain quotas (per-phase):
- Canary (us-west-2): drain max 10 GPUs (1.5% regional capacity)
- Phase A (per-region initial): drain batches up to 12% of region capacity with at least 30% buffer remaining in each availability zone
- Phase B (ramp): additional batches up to 30% total drained concurrently per region if metrics hold
- Emergency stop: immediate halt if latency P95 increases >20% over baseline or error rate spike >1.5% absolute

Planned timetable (local times):
- Canary: 2025-11-03 02:00 - 06:00 PST (us-west-2)
- Phase A - us-east-1: 2025-11-05 01:00 - 08:00 EST
- Phase A - eu-west-1: 2025-11-07 03:00 - 09:00 GMT
- Phase A - asia-southeast-1: 2025-11-09 01:00 - 06:00 ICT
- Phase B (regional ramp windows): 2025-11-10 to 2025-11-14 nightly windows (region-local low traffic hours)
- Post-rollout verification: 2025-11-15 to 2025-11-17

Per-region capacity drain matrix (example snapshot):
- us-west-2: total GPUs=6400; Phase A batch size=768 (12%); safe buffer=1920 (30%)
- us-east-1: total GPUs=7200; Phase A batch size=864; safe buffer=2160
- eu-west-1: total GPUs=2800; Phase A batch size=336; safe buffer=840
- asia-southeast-1: total GPUs=1200; Phase A batch size=144; safe buffer=360
Notes: actual batch sizes will be recomputed at T-48h from live capacity numbers; the above are planning targets.

Draining strategy (step-by-step):
1) Mark nodes for drain (kube cordon + taint) tagged with maintenance window id (maint-2025-11-driver).
2) Migrate active sessions: use graceful eviction with 5 minute attempt windows; if inference request cannot finish, the request will be retried by the API layer to fallback pool (see fallback policies).
3) Reclaim cached KV to persistent cache where applicable to avoid cold-start re-uploads.
4) Verify queue lengths and GPU utilization fall to <10% before powering node down for driver update.
5) Run automated node image update + driver install + runtime smoke tests.
6) Rejoin node to pool and validate KV cache vs baseline.

Fallback policies during maintenance:
- Route failing requests to: (1) compatible model variant on remaining GPUs, (2) lower-cost instance group with auto-quantization, (3) paused queues respond with 429 when retries exhausted per API SLAs.
- Prefer model-variant fallback that preserves shape and token limits to reduce downstream app regression.

Testing & verification checklist (automated + manual):
- Automated:
  - Unit runtime checks (latency microbenchmarks), sample generation correctness tests, kv-cache warm-up timelines
  - Synthetic traffic bursts: 1x, 2x, and 4x baseline concurrency for 30m each
  - End-to-end pipeline smoke: embedding writes, chat sessions, and streaming chunk integrity
- Manual:
  - Sampling of customer chat sessions (internal canaries)
  - Live dashboard inspection (token-level cost, P95, P99, error counts)

Monitoring signals and thresholds (stop criteria):
- Latency: P95 > baseline * 1.20 -> PAUSE rollout and investigate
- Error rate: request errors > baseline + 1.5% absolute -> PAUSE
- Throughput: token throughput < baseline * 0.70 for more than 15 minutes -> PAUSE
- System health: node reboot loops > 3 in 1 hour -> ROLLBACK pool to previous image

Rollback procedure (fast path):
- If stop criteria triggered during a batch, immediately:
  1) Abort any further drains in region.
  2) Reboot updated nodes back to previous driver image via golden snapshot (immediate rollback script).
  3) Re-inject traffic to the restored pool, monitor 30 minutes before resuming.
- If canary fails: hold campaign, revert all canary nodes, open a postmortem ticket JIRA-OPS-1987 and notify customers per comms plan.

Comms templates and notification plan:
- Internal (Slack): #infra-maintenance alert at T-24h with planned batches, at T-1h start update, and T+post window status.
- Customer-facing (email + status page): publish expected windows T-72h (informational), T-24h (reminder) and T+1h (completion summary). Use the standard incident playbook for any SLA-impacting degradation.
- On-call routing: primary infra oncall (Arjun Patel) -> secondary (Helena Ruiz) -> eng-sre pager.

Operational runbook (quick commands):
- Mark drain: kubectl label node <node> maintenance=maint-2025-11-driver && kubectl cordon <node>
- Evict pods gracefully: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300
- Re-image and install driver: /opt/infra/scripts/install-driver-570.sh --validate
- Healthcheck: /opt/infra/scripts/node-smoke.sh && curl -sS http://localhost:8080/health | jq .status

Post-maintenance verification and artifacts to collect:
- 48h metric comparison report (P50/P95/P99, error counts, token throughput) per region
- Node-level logs for updated nodes (syslog, nvidia-smi x output, driver install logs)
- List of rollbacks and root causes captured in JIRA

Open questions and pre-reqs (T-72h actions):
- Confirm golden snapshot images for each GPU type and AZ (owner: Noah Fischer).
- Recompute live batch sizes at T-48h (owner: Priya Kapoor).
- Validate fallback model variants are warmed and tested (owner: Helena Ruiz).
- Ensure runbooks and escalations are posted to confluence: driver-upgrade-playbook-2025 (owner: Maya Chen).
